overview.title: Replace a script's settings from the command line
overview.summary: Executed by train.py and sample.py so a config file or flags overwrite their global settings.

sections.title: A path is executed; a flag overwrites one name
sections.pseudocode:
An argument without = is a config file. Print it, then run it in the caller's globals.
A --key=value flag parses the value and stores it, but only if the key and its type already exist.
# Insight: This is why config/train_shakespeare_char.py can replace train.py's defaults without being imported.

logic.title: Replace a script's settings from the command line
logic.summary: Run inside train.py or sample.py and override their globals from a config file or --key=value flags.

sections.title: Run a config file, or override one global
sections.pseudocode:
Look at each argument after the script name.
If the argument has no equals sign:
    Refuse a flag that forgot its value.
    Print the config file.
    Run that file in this same global scope.
Otherwise:
    Require a --key=value flag.
    Split off the key, and drop the two dashes.
    If that key is not already a global, fail.
    Parse the value as a literal when it is a bool, number, or other Python literal.
    If parsing fails, keep the raw string.
    Require the new type to match the old one.
    Print the override and store it on globals.
# Why: Running the file here, instead of importing it, lets its assignments hit train.py's own variables.
# Insight: --block_size=256 works only because block_size already exists. A typo is an error, not a new setting.
# Context: literal_eval reads Python values such as True, 64, or 1e-3. It does not execute arbitrary code. The config file does.
